The '''2017–18 Georgia State Panthers men's basketball team''' represented [[Georgia State University]] during the [[2017–18 NCAA Division I men's basketball season]]. The team's head coach was [[Ron Hunter]], who was in his seventh season at Georgia State. The Panthers played their home games at the [[GSU Sports Arena]] in [[Atlanta|Atlanta, Georgia]] as members of the [[Sun Belt Conference]]. They finished the season 24–11, 12–6 in Sun Belt play to finish the regular season in second place. The Panthers defeated [[2017–18 Troy Trojans men's basketball team|Troy]], [[2017–18 Georgia Southern Eagles men's basketball team|Georgia Southern]], and [[2017–18 Texas–Arlington Mavericks men's basketball team|UT Arlington]] to become champions of the [[2018 Sun Belt Conference men's basketball tournament|Sun Belt tournament]]. As a result, they received the Sun Belt's automatic bid to the [[2018 NCAA Division I men's basketball tournament|NCAA tournament]]. As the No. 15 seed in the West region, they lost to [[2017–18 Cincinnati Bearcats men's basketball team|Cincinnati]] in the first round.

== Previous season ==
The [[2016–17 Georgia State Panthers men's basketball team|Panthers]] finished the [[2016–17 NCAA Division I men's basketball season|2016–17 season]] 20–13, 12–6 in Sun Belt play to finish in second place. They lost in the semifinals of the [[2017 Sun Belt Conference men's basketball tournament|Sun Belt tournament]] to [[2016–17 Troy Trojans men's basketball team|Troy]] before receiving an invitation to the [[CollegeInsider.com Postseason Tournament|CIT]], where they lost to [[2016–17 Texas A&M–Corpus Christi Islanders men's basketball team|Texas A&M Corpus Christi]].

==Preseason==
* Georgia State was picked to finish second in the Sun Belt Conference preseason coaches poll.
* Sophomore, D'Marcus Simonds, was named to the All-Sun Belt Preseason Second Team.
* On November 6, 2017, D'Marcus Simonds was named to the [[Lute Olson Award|Lute Olson National Player of the Year Award]] preseason watchlist.<ref>{{cite web|title=The Preseason Watch List|url=http://www.luteolsonaward.com/|website=Lute Olson National Player of the Year Award|accessdate=7 November 2017}}</ref>

==Regular season==
* During the November 10th game vs. Carver Bible College, D'Marcus Simonds became the first player in Georgia State history to earn a triple-double, scoring 20 points while adding 10 assists and 10 rebounds.<ref>{{cite web|last1=Holmes|first1=Mike|title=Simonds Records Triple-Double; Panthers Cruise to 90-50 Win|url=http://www.georgiastatesports.com/ViewArticle.dbml?DB_OEM_ID=12700&ATCLID=211684835|website=GeorgiaStateSports.com|publisher=Georgia State University|accessdate=13 November 2017}}</ref>
* On November 20, in a 68–50 win over Eastern Washington, [[Ron Hunter]] earned the 400th win of his career.<ref>{{cite web|last1=Holmes|first1=Mike|title=Panthers Top EWU 68-50; Hunter Earns 400th Career Win|url=http://www.georgiastatesports.com/ViewArticle.dbml?DB_OEM_ID=12700&ATCLID=211686556|website=GeorgiaStateSports.com|publisher=Georgia State University|accessdate=22 November 2017}}</ref>
* D'Marcus Simonds was named to the Lute Olson National Player of the Year Award mid-season watchlist.<ref>{{cite web|last1=Holmes|first1=Mike|title=Simonds Named to Lou Henson Mid-Season Watch List|url=https://www.nmnathletics.com/ViewArticle.dbml?DB_OEM_ID=12700&ATCLID=211692399|website=GeorgiaStateSports.com|publisher=Georgia State University|accessdate=18 January 2018}}</ref>
* On January 20, in an 83–66 win over Georgia Southern, Isaiah Williams scored his 1,000th career point.<ref>{{cite web|last1=Holmes|first1=Mike|title=Panthers Top In-State Foe Georgia Southern 83-66|url=http://www.georgiastatesports.com/ViewArticle.dbml?DB_OEM_ID=12700&ATCLID=211693550|website=GeorgiaStateSports.com|publisher=Georgia State University|accessdate=21 January 2018}}</ref>
* In a win at Little Rock on February 3, Devin Mitchell set a new scoring record for the [[Jack Stephens Center]] with his career-high 38 points.<ref>{{cite web|last1=Holmes|first1=Mike|title=Mitchell's 38 Points Lead Panthers to 81–51 Win|url=http://www.georgiastatesports.com/ViewArticle.dbml?DB_OEM_ID=12700&ATCLID=211695663|website=GeorgiaStateSports.com|publisher=Georgia State University|accessdate=3 February 2018}}</ref>
* On March 5, D'Marcus Simonds was named [[Sun Belt Conference Men's Basketball Player of the Year|Sun Belt Player of the Year]], along with All-Sun Belt First Team honors. And junior, Devin Mitchell, was named to the All-Sun Belt Third Team.<ref>{{cite web|last1=Holmes|first1=Mike|title=Simonds Named Sun Belt POTY; Mitchell Earns Third Team|url=http://www.georgiastatesports.com/ViewArticle.dbml?DB_OEM_ID=12700&ATCLID=211704250|website=GeorgiaStateSports.com|publisher=Georgia State University|accessdate=10 March 2018}}</ref>

===Sun Belt Tournament===
[[File:Georgia_State_Sun_Belt_Tournament_Champions.jpg|right|thumb|300px|The Georgia State Men's Basketball team celebrates winning the Sun Belt Conference tournament]]
After locking in the second seed in the Sun Belt Tournament, the Panthers' performance dipped in the last part of their regular season– dropping four of their final six games.<ref>{{cite web|title=BRACKET|url=https://www.cbssports.com/collegebasketball/tournaments/conference/BELT/sun-belt-tournament-bracket|website=CBSSports.com|publisher=CBS|accessdate=13 March 2018}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|title=Men's Basketball - 2017-18 Schedule|url=http://www.georgiastatesports.com/SportSelect.dbml?&DB_OEM_ID=12700&SPID=5655&SPSID=53529|website=GeorgiaStateSports.com|publisher=Georgia State University|accessdate=13 March 2018}}</ref> Able to shake free of that trend, Georgia State would beat Troy handily in the second round, 73–51, after losing to them twice in the regular season. 
In their semifinal game, the Panthers were once again pitted against in-state foe, Georgia Southern. The teams split their regular season contests– each winning at home. On this neutral court, GSU would defeat the Eagles 73–67 and eliminate their rival from the SBC Tournament for the second time in four years.<ref name="SBC Semifinal" /> This rivalry game wouldn't end without some theatrics– with less than a minute to play, Georgia Southern cut State's lead to just three points. The Panthers held the ball while the [[shot clock]] ran down to two seconds, at which point the Eagles were called for a kicked ball off of an attempted Georgia State pass. As a result, the shot clock would reset to 20 seconds– with just 23 seconds left on the game clock. The Panthers called a time out, where Coach [[Ron Hunter|Hunter]] said he reminded his team of the new shot clock differential and instructed them to hold the ball until fouled should they successfully inbound the ball.<ref>{{cite web|last1=McQuade|first1=Alec|title=GSU Panthers 1 win away from NCAA tournament thanks to a really dumb shot|url=http://www.11alive.com/article/sports/ncaab/gsu-panthers-1-win-away-from-ncaa-tournament-thanks-to-a-really-dumb-shot/85-527524602|website=11alive|publisher=NBC|accessdate=13 March 2018}}</ref> Once play resumed, the inbound pass was received by junior Devin Mitchell, who would later claim he thought Coach Hunter was talking about the game clock, and therefore still thought only two seconds remained on the shot clock, leading him to immediately turn around and shoot the ball from outside of the [[Three-point field goal|three-point arc]] and sink an unnecessary three-pointer.<ref>{{cite web|last1=Bradley|first1=Mark|title=Thanks to the greatest bad shot ever, Georgia State is dancing|url=https://www.myajc.com/blog/mark-bradley/thanks-the-greatest-bad-shot-ever-georgia-state-dancing/oeXHebiLGqGpEws7uTq8FK/|website=Atlanta Journal-Constitution|publisher=Cox Communications|accessdate=13 March 2018}}</ref> This mishap would ice the game, sending the Panthers to the SBC Tournament finals. Meanwhile, top-seeded (and regular season champions) Louisiana dropped their semifinal game to 5th seed UT-Arlington, sending the Mavericks, a team Georgia State lost to just five games earlier, to face the Panthers in the finals.<ref>{{cite web|title=Texas-Arlington vs. Georgia State odds: Sun Belt championship game picks from Vegas legend on 41-25 run|url=https://www.cbssports.com/college-basketball/news/texas-arlington-vs-georgia-state-odds-sun-belt-championship-game-picks-from-vegas-legend-on-41-25-run/|website=CBSSports.com|publisher=CBS|accessdate=13 March 2018}}</ref>
The Panthers would handle UT-Arlington in the finals with relative ease, beating them 74–61, with the help of D'Marcus Simonds' game-high 27 points. Their SBC Tournament victory would give the Panthers the Sun Belt Conferences' automatic bid to the [[2018 NCAA Division I men's basketball tournament|NCAA tournament]]. Selected as a 15-seed, Georgia State was matched with the 2nd-seeded [[2017–18 Cincinnati Bearcats men's basketball team|Cincinnati Bearcats]] for their opening game in Nashville, TN.<ref>{{cite web|last1=Holmes|first1=Mike|title=Panthers Win Sun Belt Championship; Top UTA 74-61|url=http://www.georgiastatesports.com/ViewArticle.dbml?ATCLID=211705391&DB_OEM_ID=12700|website=GeorgiaStateSports.com|publisher=Georgia State University|accessdate=13 March 2018}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|last1=Moore|first1=Ben|title=Georgia State to Face Cincinnati in NCAA Tournament|url=https://247sports.com/college/georgia-state/article/georgia-state-basketball-panthers-will-face-cincinnati-in-ncaa-tournament-116117938/|website=PantherTalk.com|publisher=247Sports|access-date=13 March 2018}}</ref>
